payload.field_feedback: Rich, and mostly critical - the field is the owner using the system. (1) TWO FEATURES SHIPPED THAT DO NOT MATCH THE DESIGN DOCUMENT, which is the reason this iteration exists: i8 built only the ntfy action-button rung of the §11 adjudication ladder while §18 records the rich hosted brief as already built and verified, and the close-and-merge split of §4 had no implementation at all until i5d. The owner ruled the standing correction: while v2 still ports from v1, always read the design document AND v1's implementation before scoping. (2) THE ACTION BUTTON WAS BROKEN, found by the owner's own tap: the lane builds url "answer:<topic>", which is not a URL scheme, so ntfy answered 'Expected URL scheme http or https but was answer'. The design doc had flagged that exact leg as never verified. (3) GUARDS MUST BE WHITELISTS, ruled after the same failure shape appeared twice in one day - name the one accepted state, treat everything else as failure, exactly as the state machine treats legal transitions. (4) AN IMPORT IS READ-ONLY, whatever the mechanism, ruled after an npm file: symlink let a worktree removal delete the imported benjamin repository. (5) PHONE PUBLISH IS ABOUT WHO BLESSES: an unattended self-blessing run needs no phone traffic, but a gate the owner is meant to adjudicate must always reach the phone, because they may not be at the machine. (6) POSITIVE: the from-away bless WORKS - the owner blessed i5d's release gate from their phone, hash-bound, recorded channel=phone.

payload.waste_leads: The expensive waste this session was REWORK CAUSED BY NOT READING THE DESIGN DOC FIRST - i8's phone lane has to be redone (this iteration), and i5d had to implement a §4 section that had been specified for months. Both were avoidable by reading before scoping. Second: three test suites had to be reconciled after the close moved to the bless path, which was honest work but would have been cheaper if the close had been wired where iterations actually close from the start. Third, smaller: my own verification scripts twice had shell-quoting bugs that produced misleading output (a literal backslash-n split, and a PowerShell quoting failure), which cost a diagnosis round each.
payload.process_stale: YES, and specifically. The process let two features ship without ever being compared against the design document that specifies them, and it let a leg ship that the design document itself listed as unverified. Nothing in the machine asks 'what does the design document already rule about this, and what did v1 already do?' The owner has now ruled that as a standing law while the port continues; the durable fix is that the framing milestones must cite the design doc's relevant sections and v1's implementation, so the reconciliation is evidence rather than memory. That belongs in the machine's guidance, not in an agent's head, and this iteration will demonstrate it by grounding its own frame in §11, §18, §19 and v1's ask.go.
